column1: Tighter financial and credit conditions—reinforced by the 5.25–5.50% policy rate and ongoing balance-sheet runoff—are likely to weigh on demand, hiring, and inflation. Consistent with Bernanke, Gertler, and Gilchrist’s financial-accelerator mechanism, higher external finance premia can amplify the drag on activity, while Clarida, Galí, and Gertler’s work on policy rules and transmission suggests disinflation will materialize with lags; QT-related term-premium effects (Cochrane–Piazzesi) add further restraint. With the banking system sound and lender-of-last-resort backstops in place (Bagehot tradition), systemic risk appears contained even as growth-at-risk tilts modestly negative and the right tail of inflation-at-risk narrows. sentiment score = -0.12
